title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-emma-li
content:
Quick dump of notes from PR review + follow-ups (PR 4721 + related). Mostly for my own memory and to hand off to Ravi / Samir. // High-level: goal is to reduce tail latency regressions introduced by continuous-batching changes and make KV cache behavior more explicit across model variants.

Summary of what I saw:
- PR 4721 introduces dynamic batching rework + upstream kv-cache refactor (split cache manager + batch coordinator). Looks like a good cleanup but a couple of risky callsites where we now access cache asynchronously without explicit invalidation.
- Microbenchmarks (local) show 95th p99 increases from ~120ms -> ~180ms on short seq (32) workloads when batching factor spikes. Avg token time unaffected. Might be due to ordering/locking contention or IO spikes on cache misses.
- Related PR 5890 (optimizer tweaks) changed default max-batch-window from 15ms -> 25ms; could amplify batching windows and make p99 worse.

Concrete review checklist (what I validated / still need to validate):
- [x] Verify unit tests updated for new cache manager boundaries (cache_ttl tests): pass on Linux x86.
- [x] Run integration smoke with openai-compat endpoint: OK for simple generation.
- [ ] Reproduce perf regression on a 4-GPU dev rig (steps below).
- [ ] Add deterministic repro in perf harness for short sequences and burst arrivals.
- [ ] Add targeted concurrency test that simulates cache miss storms with batching enabled.

Repro steps I left in a script (todo: push to repo under infra/perf):
1) Start local runtime with --batch-window-ms=25 --max-batch-size=64 and kv-cache enabled.
2) Use loadgen script (scripts/loadgen-shortseq.py) to send 3000 requests with poisson arrival, lambda tuned to hit concurrency 40-60.
3) Collect p50/p95/p99 and cpu/gpu utilization and lock contention traces.
Notes: initial run on my laptop container (4vCPU) produced similar p99 bump but noisy; need a real GPU machine.

Potential root causes (brainstorm):
- Locking contention in CacheManager::get_or_create when many small batches try to read/update the same prefix entry. We used a single big mutex previously, refactor might have introduced fine-grained locks but non-optimal ordering -> convoys.
- Increased batch-window increases simultaneous outstanding requests which expose race on warmup path (async kv fetch misses then writeback).
- Hash-sharding of cache entries not covering hot keys; hot keys concentrate to single shard under current hash, lacking randomization.
- GC / cleanup path runs synchronously on misses (maybe moved from background thread).

Suggested code changes / experiments:
- Reintroduce read-path fast-path: check atomic presence flag before taking any lock. Quick return for hits. (low-risk, high-reward)
- Move expensive cleanup to background worker or defer using a queue.
- Add per-shard metrics (misses, locks wait time) to help identify hot shards.
- Consider jittering batch-window per request class to avoid synchronized batching storms.

Tests / TODOs to add to repo (filenames tentative):
- tests/kv_cache/concurrency_repro_test.py -> deterministic seed + fake time to simulate bursts.
- tests/perf/integration_shortseq_batching.py -> runs in CI perf cluster nightly.
- Add stress job in infra/perf that runs scaled scenario (100k requests) and emits traces to jaeger.

Follow-ups for PR / assignees:
- Ravi: run the 4-GPU repro and attach perf traces here. Please pin kernel version and nvidia driver in notes. (Ravi assigned)
- Samir: look into cache shard hash function and add telemetry. If hot-key skew confirmed, propose quick fix (add salt).
- Avery: check if optimizer PR 5890 should revert default batch-window or expose as feature flag to customer.
- Me (Emma): write the deterministic test and add the read-path fast-path; prototype in a small branch.

Open questions / things to call out in review comment:
- Is there an expectation that cache cleanup remains synchronous? If so, we should document performance implications in code comments.
- Are there model variants (e.g., long-context models) where cache semantics changed after refactor? Need explicit compatibility test matrix.
- Should we add a rollout guard (canary) for this change in Dedicated to avoid wide blast radius? I think yes.

Draft PR comment (copy/paste):
"Thanks for the cleanup — overall nice separation of concerns. I have a few perf/regression concerns on p99 for short-sequence workloads when batching windows increase. I recommend adding a read fast-path to avoid locking on hits, deferring cleanup to background, and adding per-shard metrics to pinpoint hot keys. Also please include a deterministic perf test so we can guard against regressions. Assigning follow-ups: Ravi (repro + traces), Samir (telemetry & hash), Avery (batch-window default)."

Random notes to self:
- remember to check infra/perf VM kernel settings (tcp_tw_reuse?) — network stack can affect short request bursts.
- link back to old design doc: confluence link above (was helpful to compare).
- small patch for fast-path might live under serving-runtime/src/cache/fast_path.{cc,hh}

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and convert to a proper PR checklist once repro is confirmed.
